note: Two real bugs found and fixed during this stage: (1) idempotent-cleanup DELETE statements on three FTS5 virtual tables with no usable index on content_sha256 caused a full-table scan on every newly-ingested file, getting slower as the tables grew -- removed since they only ever ran on genuinely-new content, where nothing exists yet to delete; (2) a rare SQLite write-lock contention case under 8 concurrent workers could exhaust even the last-resort fallback row write, silently dropping up to 195 files from the catalogue while an in-memory counter still looked internally consistent -- fixed by giving that specific fallback write a longer (20s) busy_timeout. Verified by direct disk-vs-database comparison, not just the self-reported residual, after each fix.
